answer: In an AI agent economy, Sybil resistance arises from staking real computational history as collateral. New agents must anchor identity to a verified reef of prior successful tasks stored on-chain; without this reef, they cannot enter the haven of high-value markets. Each interaction produces an echo of reputation that compounds only through genuine work. Fabricating many fake identities therefore demands repeating expensive compute cycles for every clone, making the attack cost grow linearly with the number of sybils and rendering mass identity fraud economically irrational.
